articles.title: Crorepati investors touch record Rs 10 lakh crore milestone. Which stocks are making them richer?
articles.content: HNIs’ holdings in NSE-listed stocks surged 22.55% QoQ to a record Rs 9.92 lakh crore by June-end, adding Rs 1.83 lakh crore in three months. Their share of market value rose to 2.12%, the highest since March 2022. However, average ownership by volume fell to 7.19% from 7.31%, suggesting the rise was driven largely by stock price gains and greater exposure to high-value companies rather than fresh buying.

articles.title: Hindustan Copper shares in focus as OFS opens for retail investors. Here are all the details
articles.content: Hindustan Copper’s government OFS drew strong institutional demand, with the non-retail portion subscribed 3.41 times on Tuesday. The company’s strong Q1 performance and plans to expand mining capacity also remain in focus.

articles.title: Decoding gold rally: Why yellow metal surged 15% in one month and should bullion be in your portfolio?

articles.title: Dollar moves in a narrow range ahead of inflation data, Jackson Hole
articles.content: In Asian markets, the dollar held steady as traders looked ahead to crucial inflation reports, particularly the US PCE data set to be released before the Jackson Hole symposium this weekend. Meanwhile, oil prices dipped due to easing tensions in the Middle East and halted diplomatic negotiations. The Australian dollar strengthened following favorable inflation figures, while cryptocurrencies continued their upward trajectory, and gold saw a minor decline.

articles.title: Yes, Federal, RBL put dollar bond plans on hold
articles.content: Yes Bank withdrew its dollar debt plan as investors sought higher yields. Federal Bank and RBL Bank also postponed their dollar bond issuances. These lenders await a more favorable time to raise necessary foreign currency. An oversupply of Indian bonds has increased investor demand for better returns. This situation impacts the banks' ability to secure international funding.

articles.title: Gold little changed with US inflation data in spotlight
articles.content: Gold prices held steady as investors kept a watchful eye on upcoming United States inflation data, which is expected to offer insights into the Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions. Market participants are looking towards a potential pause in rate hikes next month. Concurrently, other precious metals, including silver, platinum, and palladium, experienced slight increases, reflecting ongoing global economic concerns and trade tensions impacting market dynamics.

articles.title: Oil prices slide 2% on Iran-Oman talks to reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.content: Oil prices have dropped following the revival of discussions between Iran and Oman regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz. The losses across both benchmarks highlight the market's reaction to navigation issues. Despite uncertainty gripping the market, some bargain buying has emerged, preventing further price decreases, while the U.S. is shifting personnel to its Middle Eastern diplomatic missions.

articles.title: Gross FDI climbs as net inflows turn positive
articles.content: Gross foreign direct investment into India saw a significant rise in June.  Net FDI also increased substantially, recovering from a previous month's outflow.  Outward FDI, however, continued its downward trend for the past two months.  Financial, insurance, and business services were key sectors for outward investments.  Manufacturing and trade sectors also witnessed outward FDI activity.

articles.title: Outward remittances under LRS up at $2.5 billion
articles.content: In June, the total outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme soared to $2.5 billion. Notably, Indians disbursed $1.3 billion on international travel, reflecting a significant uptick from the previous month. Meanwhile, expenditure on overseas education rose to $96 million. Additionally, remittances for the upkeep of close relatives accounted for $287 million, while investments in equity and debt attracted $456 million from Indian residents.

articles.title: Axis Bank set to raise $700 million through ECB swap facility
articles.content: Axis Bank is set to secure seven hundred million dollars through a dedicated external commercial borrowing facility. This loan features two tranches with tenures of three and five years. The arrangement is spearheaded by CTBC Bank from Taiwan and United Overseas Bank from Singapore, with significant contributions from the World Bank's IFC. Additional banks are anticipated to participate as the syndication phase unfolds.
